question.text: What is the significance of an entity being 'appropriately regulated' in the context of FPI categorization?

answer.text: An applicant incorporated or established in an International Financial Services Centre is deemed to be appropriately regulated
Appropriate regulation requires registration with at least three regulatory bodies
Only entities regulated by central banks are considered appropriately regulated
Only entities regulated by SEBI are considered appropriately regulated

explanation.text: The Logic: The FPI regulations state that an applicant incorporated or established in an International Financial Services Centre (IFSC) is deemed to be appropriately regulated for FPI categorisation purposes. The Trap: "Appropriately regulated" is not narrowly limited to SEBI or central-bank oversight, and there is no numeric threshold of "three regulators". The IFSC-incorporation route is a specific deeming provision. Note: When assessing categorisation, treat IFSC incorporation as one of the recognised gateways to "appropriately regulated" status without having to layer on additional regulator counts.
